Ona stojí hneď pred mapou Slovenska.

en: Where did you go after you introduced yourself?

altSk: Písala poznámky a potom zapísala všetko.

en: My apartment costs four hundred euros.

en: I am an architect and I work from home.
sk: Som architekt a pracujem z domu.
altSk: Som architektka a pracujem z domu.

en: My apartment has three large rooms.

en: I want a warm day tomorrow.

en: The days will be long and sunny tomorrow.

Zajtra dni budú dlhé a slnečné.

theme: describing the weather yesterday and tomorrow

en: I am enjoying myself at the cinema.

en: At what time does the film start?
altSk: O ktorej hodine sa začína film?
O koľkej hodine sa začína film?

Včera sme šli do kina električkou.

hint: Use ordinal number in locative with 'o' for clock times. Tri → tretej.
theme: telling the time and making appointments

en: She could not come to the meeting yesterday.
altSk: Ona včera nemohla prísť na stretnutie.
hint: Past tense of 'môcť' for a female subject: mohla → nemohla. Add 'ne-' for negation.

en: I see my good friend Peter there.

Vidím tam môjho dobrého priateľa Petra.
Tam vidím môjho dobrého priateľa Petra.

hint: instrument/transport uses bare instrumental, no preposition: auto→autom

en: I will cook dinner at home today.

Dlho sme sa bavili o večeri.
Bavili sme sa dlho o večeri.
hint: 'O' + locative — 'večera' becomes 'večeri'.

hint: chcieť takes infinitive; 'dnešný' is a possessive adjective

hint: Use perfective 'napísať' for a completed future action; present form of perfective = future

altSk: Aké dátumy sú voľné tento týždeň?

hint: vysvetlím = perfective present acting as future

hint: Use 'ešte' + negation with past tense of 'začať sa' → nezačal sa

hint: chcieť + infinitive; zavolať is perfective

en: The white, blue and red colours are beautiful.
sk: Biele, modré a červené farby sú krásne.
altSk: Farby biela, modrá a červená sú krásne.
Tieto farby — biela, modrá a červená — sú krásne.
hint: Adjectives in plural nominative end in '-é' for neuter/feminine plural agreement with 'farby'
theme: what colours do you see in the Slovak flag?

en: She has a red dress.
hint: 'šaty' (dress) is plural neuter — adjective takes neuter plural form 'červené'

en: He is wearing a blue jacket.
sk: On má na sebe modrú bundu.
hint: 'bundu' is accusative singular feminine of 'bunda' — adjective 'modrú' agrees in accusative feminine

en: Her shoes are black.
hint: 'čierne' is a predicate adjective agreeing with 'topánky' (feminine plural nominative)

en: He is not wearing a white shirt today.
sk: Dnes nemá na sebe bielu košeľu.
altSk: On dnes nemá na sebe bielu košeľu.
hint: 'košeľu' is accusative singular feminine; 'bielu' agrees in accusative fem; negation uses 'nemá'
focus: accusative negative (fem sg) + colour adjective agreement

en: I like this dress.
altSk: Táto šatka sa mi páči veľmi.
hint: Use 'táto' (this, feminine nominative) + noun. 'Páčiť sa' is reflexive.
theme: comparing two outfits in a fitting room

en: The skirt is short, not long.
altSk: Tá sukňa je krátka, nie dlhá.
hint: Use adjective opposite pair: krátky/dlhý, agree with feminine noun 'sukňa'.
theme: comparing two outfits in a fitting room

en: Do you like it? I think it is wide.
sk: Páči sa ti? Myslím, že je široká.
altSk: Páči sa ti? Myslím, že je veľmi široká.
Páči sa ti to? Myslím, že je široká.
hint: Use adjective opposite: úzky/široký. 'široká' agrees with a feminine noun (e.g. sukňa/košeľa).
theme: comparing two outfits in a fitting room

en: I tried it on but I don't want it.
sk: Vyskúšal som ho, ale nechcem ho.
altSk: Vyskúšala som ho, ale nechcem ho.
Vyskúšal som ju, ale nechcem ju.
Vyskúšala som ju, ale nechcem ju.
hint: Use accusative pronoun 'ho' (for masc. noun, e.g. kabát) or 'ju' (for fem. noun, e.g. blúzku). Match gender of the item tried on.
theme: comparing two outfits in a fitting room

en: This dress is very elegant.
hint: 'šaty' (dress) is plural in Slovak; adjective must agree in plural
theme: comparing two outfits in a fitting room

en: I prefer the red skirt.
hint: 'sukňu' is accusative singular feminine (inanimate); adjective also takes accusative feminine ending -ú
theme: comparing two outfits in a fitting room

en: Do you usually wear a jacket?
hint: 'nosiť' is an imperfective verb meaning habitual wearing; group I conjugation: nosíš
theme: comparing two outfits in a fitting room

en: I am going to put on the blue coat, not the black one.
sk: Oblečiem si modrý kabát, nie čierny.
altSk: Oblečiem si modrý kabát, nie čierny kabát.
Dám si modrý kabát, nie čierny.
hint: 'obliecť si' is perfective; its present form 'oblečiem si' expresses future meaning; adjectives agree with 'kabát' (masculine inanimate accusative: -ý)
focus: present tense (obliecť si) as future + accusative inanimate
theme: comparing two outfits in a fitting room

en: Do you have this jacket in blue?
hint: 'túto' is accusative feminine demonstrative; 'bundu' is accusative feminine noun
theme: shopping for clothes — asking for size and colour

en: That skirt is long, but I want a short one.
sk: Tá sukňa je dlhá, ale chcem krátku.
altSk: Tá sukňa je dlhá, ale ja chcem krátku.
hint: adjective opposites dlhý/krátky; 'krátku' is accusative feminine
theme: shopping for clothes — asking for size and colour

en: I like this shirt. I will buy it.
sk: Táto košeľa sa mi páči. Kúpim ju.
altSk: Páči sa mi táto košeľa. Kúpim ju.
Táto košeľa sa mi páči. Ju kúpim.
hint: 'ju' is accusative feminine pronoun replacing 'košeľa'
theme: shopping for clothes — asking for size and colour

en: These trousers are wide, but I need narrow ones.
sk: Tieto nohavice sú široké, ale potrebujem úzke.
altSk: Tieto nohavice sú široké, ale ja potrebujem úzke.
Tieto nohavice sú široké, no potrebujem úzke.
hint: adjective opposites široký/úzky; 'tieto' is nominative plural demonstrative; 'úzke' is accusative plural adjective used as noun
theme: shopping for clothes — asking for size and colour

en: I want this winter coat.
hint: 'coat' (kabát) is masculine inanimate, so accusative = nominative form; 'tento' → 'tento' (masc. inanim. acc.)
theme: buying a winter coat in a Slovak shop

en: Is this coat warm and long?
sk: Je tento kabát teplý a dlhý?
altSk: Tento kabát je teplý a dlhý?
hint: adjectives 'teplý' and 'dlhý' must agree with masculine nominative 'kabát'
theme: buying a winter coat in a Slovak shop

en: I am trying on a black winter coat.
altSk: Ja si obliekam čierny zimný kabát.
hint: reflexive verb 'obliekať si' (to try on/put on); 'si' is the reflexive particle; 'čierny' agrees with masculine inanimate accusative 'kabát'
focus: present tense of reflexive verb obliekať si
theme: buying a winter coat in a Slovak shop

en: Do you usually wear a warm coat in winter?
sk: Nosíš zvyčajne teplý kabát v zime?
altSk: Zvyčajne nosíš teplý kabát v zime?
Nosíš teplý kabát v zime zvyčajne?
hint: 'nosiť' (to wear/carry habitually) conjugated for 'ty'; 'v zime' = locative of 'zima' (in winter); 'teplý kabát' = masculine inanimate accusative
focus: present tense of nosiť + locative time expression
theme: buying a winter coat in a Slovak shop

en: I am buying a new jacket.
hint: accusative singular feminine: nová bunda → novú bundu
theme: getting dressed for a job interview

en: She wants to wear a white blouse.
altSk: Ona chce obliecť si bielu blúzku.
Ona chce si obliecť bielu blúzku.
hint: chcieť + infinitive; colour adjective biela → bielu in accusative
theme: getting dressed for a job interview

en: He is putting on a dark blue suit.
hint: accusative masculine inanimate: tmavomodrý oblek (no ending change); reflexive si with obliekať sa
theme: getting dressed for a job interview

en: Do you want to buy black shoes?
altSk: Ty si chceš kúpiť čierne topánky?
hint: question with chcieť + infinitive kúpiť; accusative plural feminine: čierne topánky
focus: modal chcieť + infinitive in a question; accusative plural
theme: getting dressed for a job interview

en: I wear a warm jacket in winter.
altSk: V zime si obliekam teplú bundu.
Obliekam si teplú bundu v zime.
hint: 'bunda' (jacket) is feminine accusative singular — teplá → teplú bundu
focus: adjective agreement with clothing noun (feminine accusative sg)
theme: what to wear in different Slovak weather

en: He is putting on a red scarf today.
hint: 'šál' is masculine inanimate accusative — červený šál (no change from nominative form in masc. inanimate acc.)
theme: what to wear in different Slovak weather

en: Do you wear a hat when it is cold?
altSk: Obliekaš si čiapku, keď je chladno?
Keď je chladno, obliekaš si čiapku?
hint: 'čiapka' is feminine accusative singular — čiapka → čiapku; question without question word
focus: present tense (nosiť / obliecť si) + feminine accusative sg
theme: what to wear in different Slovak weather

en: We do not put on light clothes in cold weather.
sk: V chladnom počasí si neobliekame ľahké oblečenie.
altSk: Neobliekame si ľahké oblečenie v chladnom počasí.
V chladnom počasí nenosíme ľahké oblečenie.
Nenosíme ľahké oblečenie v chladnom počasí.
hint: 'chladnom počasí' is locative (v + locative); 'ľahké oblečenie' is neuter accusative sg; double negation: neobliekame si
focus: adjective agreement in locative (v chladnom počasí) + neuter accusative + negation
theme: what to wear in different Slovak weather

en: I am packing a suitcase.
hint: 'balit'' is a regular verb; 'kufor' (suitcase) is masculine, accusative singular — same form as nominative
theme: packing a suitcase for a weekend trip

en: I will buy a blue jacket.
hint: colour adjective 'modrý' → feminine accusative 'modrú'; 'bunda' → accusative 'bundu'; 'kúpim' is perfective present used as future
theme: packing a suitcase for a weekend trip

en: I want to pack a red T-shirt.
altSk: Ja chcem si zabaliť červené tričko.
hint: 'chcieť' + infinitive; 'červený' → neuter accusative 'červené'; 'tričko' (T-shirt) is neuter, accusative same as nominative
focus: modal chcieť + infinitive with colour adjective in accusative (neuter)
theme: packing a suitcase for a weekend trip

en: Did you pack your black shoes?
hint: past tense of 'zbaliť': masculine 'zbalil' / feminine 'zbalila'; 'čierny' → plural accusative 'čierne'; 'topánky' (shoes) are feminine plural, accusative plural 'topánky'
focus: past tense question + colour adjective in accusative plural
theme: packing a suitcase for a weekend trip

en: She is wearing a red dress.
hint: 'šaty' (dress) is inanimate accusative plural; adjective matches: červené šaty
focus: adjective agreement with clothing noun (inanimate accusative plural)
theme: describing what people are wearing at a party

en: Do you see that man in the blue suit?
sk: Vidíš toho muža v modrom obleku?
altSk: Vidíš tamtoho muža v modrom obleku?
hint: 'muža' is animate accusative singular of 'muž'; 'toho' is the animate accusative demonstrative pronoun
theme: describing what people are wearing at a party

en: Peter is putting on a white shirt now.
sk: Peter si teraz oblieka bielu košeľu.
altSk: Peter si oblieka teraz bielu košeľu.
Teraz si Peter oblieka bielu košeľu.
hint: 'obliekať si' is the imperfective reflexive verb meaning to put on/be putting on; 'bielu košeľu' is inanimate accusative singular
focus: present tense of reflexive verb obliekať si
theme: describing what people are wearing at a party

en: They are not wearing elegant clothes tonight.
sk: Dnes večer si neobliekajú elegantné oblečenie.
hint: double negation not needed here but 'ne-' prefix on verb; 'elegantné oblečenie' is inanimate accusative singular; time expression 'dnes večer' typically opens the sentence
focus: negative present tense with clothing in accusative
theme: describing what people are wearing at a party

en: I am a teacher.
hint: Use 'som' + profession noun (no article needed). Choose učiteľ (male) or učiteľka (female).
focus: profession with byť — nominative noun, no article
theme: talking about what you want to be

en: She is not a doctor.
hint: Negate 'je' with 'nie je'. Profession stays in nominative. Subject pronoun is optional.
focus: negation with byť + feminine profession noun
theme: talking about what you want to be

en: What do you do? I am an engineer.
hint: Use 'robíš' (informal) or 'robíte' (formal/plural). Answer with 'som' + profession.
theme: talking about what you want to be

en: He wants to be a police officer.
hint: Use modal 'chcieť' (chce = he/she wants) + infinitive 'byť' + profession in nominative.
theme: talking about what you want to be

en: My mother is a doctor.
hint: Use 'lekárka' (feminine form) with 'je' — no article needed in Slovak

en: My brother is a teacher, not a doctor.
sk: Môj brat je učiteľ, nie lekár.
hint: Masculine profession forms: 'učiteľ', 'lekár' — no feminine endings here

en: What do you do? I am an engineer.
hint: 'Čo robíte?' = polite/plural; 'Čo robíš?' = informal singular; answer with 'Som + profession'

en: My parents were not teachers, they were nurses.
sk: Moji rodičia neboli učitelia, boli zdravotníci.
altSk: Moji rodičia neboli učiteľmi, boli zdravotníkmi.
hint: Past tense of 'byť': 'neboli' (they were not); nominative plural: 'učitelia', 'zdravotníci'; instrumental plural also possible: 'učiteľmi', 'zdravotníkmi'
focus: past tense of byť + double negation + nominative/instrumental plural

en: I am a doctor, not a teacher.
hint: Use 'som' for 'I am'; profession after 'byť' is in nominative (no article needed)

en: She is a good teacher.
hint: Adjective 'dobrá' must agree with feminine noun 'učiteľka' in nominative singular

en: Are you a doctor or a nurse?
altSk: Ty si lekár alebo zdravotná sestra?
Ty si doktor alebo zdravotná sestra?
hint: Use 'si' for 'you are' (singular informal); both professions stay in nominative after 'byť'
focus: present byť (si) + nominative profession in question

en: He is not a bad engineer, but she is a great architect.
sk: On nie je zlý inžinier, ale ona je skvelá architektka.
altSk: Nie je zlý inžinier, ale ona je skvelá architektka.
On nie je zlý inžinier, ale je skvelá architektka.
Nie je zlý inžinier, ale je skvelá architektka.
hint: Use 'nie je' for negation; adjectives 'zlý' (masc) and 'skvelá' (fem) agree with their nouns in nominative
focus: adjective + profession with negation and gender agreement

en: I am a student.
hint: Use 'som' for 'I am'; profession in nominative, no article
theme: talking about what you want to be

en: She wants to be a doctor.
hint: 'chcieť' conjugates as 'chce' for she/he/it; profession stays in nominative after 'byť'
focus: modal chcieť + infinitive byť + nominative predicate
theme: talking about what you want to be

en: He is not a teacher.
hint: Negate 'je' with 'nie je'; profession in nominative (or instrumental is also natural)
theme: talking about what you want to be

en: Do you want to be a good engineer?
hint: 'chceš' for you (singular); adjective 'dobrý' agrees with masculine noun in nominative
focus: adjective + profession in nominative + question word order
theme: talking about what you want to be

en: My mum works as a doctor.
hint: Use 'ako' + instrumental-like noun for professions (ako + nominative form in Slovak)

en: Where does your dad work?
hint: Question word 'kde' triggers present tense; verb moves early in questions

en: My brother does not work in an office.
hint: 'v kancelárii' is locative singular; negate with 'ne-' prefix on verb

en: My sister worked as a nurse in a hospital.
sk: Moja sestra pracovala ako zdravotná sestra v nemocnici.
altSk: Moja sestra robila ako zdravotná sestra v nemocnici.
Sestra pracovala ako zdravotná sestra v nemocnici.
Sestra robila ako zdravotná sestra v nemocnici.
hint: Past tense: pracovať → pracovala (fem.); 'v nemocnici' is locative; profession after 'ako'

en: I work as a doctor.
hint: Use 'ako' + nominative for professions
theme: introducing yourself and your job at a conference

en: Where do you work?
hint: 'pracovať' is a Group I verb; formal vs informal forms both valid
theme: introducing yourself and your job at a conference

en: I am a teacher and I work at a school.
sk: Som učiteľ a pracujem v škole.
altSk: Som učiteľka a pracujem v škole.
Som učiteľ a robím v škole.
Som učiteľka a robím v škole.
hint: 'v škole' uses locative; učiteľ/učiteľka depends on gender
theme: introducing yourself and your job at a conference

en: I don't work as an engineer, I work as a programmer.
sk: Nepracujem ako inžinier, pracujem ako programátor.
altSk: Nerobím ako inžinier, robím ako programátor.
Nepracujem ako inžinierka, pracujem ako programátorka.
Nerobím ako inžinierka, robím ako programátorka.
hint: Double negation not needed here; simply negate the verb with 'ne-'; swap gender forms if female speaker
focus: negation of present tense + pracovať ako + profession
theme: introducing yourself and your job at a conference

en: My mother is a doctor.
hint: Use 'je' for third person singular of byť. Profession as predicate stays in nominative.

en: Are you a teacher?
hint: Use 'si' for second person singular of byť. No article needed in Slovak.

en: My brother is not a cook.
hint: Negate byť with 'nie je'. Profession stays in nominative even in negative sentences.
focus: nominative (profession as predicate) + byť negation: nie je

en: My father is a very good engineer.
sk: Môj otec je veľmi dobrý inžinier.
altSk: Môj otec je veľmi dobrý technik.
hint: The adjective 'dobrý' must agree with the masculine noun 'inžinier' in nominative singular.

en: I am a student.
hint: Use 'som' for 'I am'; no article needed
theme: a job fair at the university

en: She is a doctor.
hint: Use 'je' for 'she is'; female doctor is 'lekárka'
theme: a job fair at the university

en: He is a good engineer.
hint: Adjective 'dobrý' agrees with masculine noun 'inžinier' in nominative
theme: a job fair at the university

en: We are not teachers.
hint: Use 'nie sme' for 'we are not'; plural masculine animate nominative 'učitelia'
focus: negation with byť + nominative plural profession
theme: a job fair at the university

en: I am from Germany.
hint: Use 'som' (I am). 'z Nemecka' = from Germany (this fixed phrase is learned as a chunk at A1).
theme: asking and saying where people live

en: Where are you from?
hint: 'Odkiaľ' = from where. Use 'ste' (formal/plural) or 'si' (informal).
theme: asking and saying where people live

en: She is not Slovak, she is Czech.
sk: Ona nie je Slovenka, ona je Češka.
altSk: Ona nie je Slovenka, je Češka.
hint: Nationality nouns must match gender: Slovenka/Češka for female. Use 'nie je' for negation.
theme: asking and saying where people live

en: Are you Italian or Spanish?
hint: Use 'si' (informal) or 'ste' (formal). Nationality nouns change for male/female: Talian/Talianka, Španiel/Španielka.
focus: nationality adjective/noun agreement + yes-no question with byť
theme: asking and saying where people live

en: She is French.
hint: Use the feminine nationality noun Francúzka (not the adjective). No article needed.
theme: an international students' meeting in Bratislava

en: He comes from Italy.
hint: nationality noun: Talian (m.) / Talianka (f.) — use 'Je Talian/Talianka' for origin
focus: present tense: pochádzať + country name Taliansko
theme: an international students' meeting in Bratislava

en: We live in Slovakia.
hint: 'na Slovensku' = in Slovakia (locative). Use 'na' with Slovensko, not 'v'. Both bývať and žiť are natural here.
focus: present tense: bývať/žiť + country name Slovensko in locative (na Slovensku)
theme: an international students' meeting in Bratislava

en: Do you live in Germany or in France?
sk: Bývaš v Nemecku alebo vo Francúzsku?
altSk: Žiješ v Nemecku alebo vo Francúzsku?
Bývate v Nemecku alebo vo Francúzsku?
Žijete v Nemecku alebo vo Francúzsku?
hint: 'v Nemecku' and 'vo Francúzsku' are locative forms. 'vo' is used before 'Fr-' cluster. Both bývať and žiť work; singular (ty) or polite plural (vy) are both natural.
focus: present tense: bývať/žiť + country names Nemecko/Francúzsko in locative
theme: an international students' meeting in Bratislava

en: She is from Spain.
hint: 'z' here is fixed in this phrase — just memorise it as a chunk. 'Ona' is optional but natural for emphasis.
theme: talking about which countries your classmates come from

en: I am not from France, I am from Slovakia.
sk: Nie som z Francúzska, som zo Slovenska.
altSk: Nie som z Francúzska, ja som zo Slovenska.
hint: Double check: 'nie som' for negation of 'byť'. 'z/zo' before country names is a fixed phrase — treat it as a chunk.
theme: talking about which countries your classmates come from

en: We live in Germany.
hint: Locative case after 'v': Nemecko → Nemecku. The pronoun 'my' is optional.
theme: talking about which countries your classmates come from

en: Do you live in Italy or in Poland?
sk: Bývaš v Taliansku alebo v Poľsku?
altSk: Ty bývaš v Taliansku alebo v Poľsku?
Bývate v Taliansku alebo v Poľsku?
hint: Locative after 'v': Taliansko → Taliansku, Poľsko → Poľsku. 'Ty' is optional; use 'bývate' for formal/plural 'you'.
theme: talking about which countries your classmates come from

en: I visited France last year.
hint: Francúzsko is the Slovak name for France (accusative, neuter). Use navštíviť (perfective) in past tense. Minulý rok = last year.
theme: describing a country you have visited

en: I am a Frenchman, but my friend is a Frenchwoman.
sk: Ja som Francúz, ale môj priateľ je Francúzka.
altSk: Som Francúz, ale môj priateľ je Francúzka.
Ja som Francúz, ale moja priateľka je Francúzka.
hint: Francúz = French man (nominative), Francúzka = French woman (nominative). Nationality nouns follow standard patterns.
theme: describing a country you have visited

en: Do you live in France or in Italy?
sk: Bývaš vo Francúzsku alebo v Taliansku?
altSk: Žiješ vo Francúzsku alebo v Taliansku?
Bývaš v Taliansku alebo vo Francúzsku?
Žiješ v Taliansku alebo vo Francúzsku?
hint: Use locative after v/vo for countries. Francúzsko→vo Francúzsku, Taliansko→v Taliansku. Bývať and žiť both mean 'to live/reside'.
focus: present tense (bývať/žiť) + country names in locative
theme: describing a country you have visited

en: She is originally from Italy, but she now lives in France.
sk: Je Talianka, ale teraz býva vo Francúzsku.
altSk: Ona pochádza z Talianska, ale teraz býva vo Francúzsku.
Pochádza z Talianska, ale teraz žije vo Francúzsku.
Ona pochádza z Talianska, ale teraz žije vo Francúzsku.
hint: nationality noun Talianka + bývať v + locative: vo Francúzsku
theme: describing a country you have visited

en: I live in Slovakia, not in France.
sk: Bývam na Slovensku, nie vo Francúzsku.
altSk: Žijem na Slovensku, nie vo Francúzsku.
hint: Use 'na Slovensku' and 'vo Francúzsku' (locative). Note: Slovakia uses 'na', not 'v'.

en: She is not from Italy, she is Slovak.
altSk: Ona nie je z Talianska, ona je Slovenka.
hint: negation of nationality: Nie je Talianka; 'je Slovenka' = she is Slovak

en: We live in Slovakia but they live in Germany.
sk: My bývame na Slovensku, ale oni bývajú v Nemecku.
altSk: Bývame na Slovensku, ale oni bývajú v Nemecku.
My žijeme na Slovensku, ale oni žijú v Nemecku.
Žijeme na Slovensku, ale oni žijú v Nemecku.
hint: Use 'my' and 'oni' for contrast. 'Bývať' group I: bývam/bývaš/býva/bývame/bývate/bývajú.

en: Are you Slovak or are you Polish?
altSk: Ty si Slovák alebo si Poliak?
hint: Use 'byť' present tense: si (ty). Nationality nouns: Slovák, Poliak (masculine).

en: I am from Italy.
hint: 'z Talianska' is a set phrase meaning 'from Italy' — just memorise it as a chunk for now
theme: a map of Europe — naming countries in Slovak

en: She is not from France, she is from Spain.
sk: Ona nie je z Francúzska, ona je zo Španielska.
altSk: Nie je z Francúzska, je zo Španielska.
Ona nie je z Francúzska, je zo Španielska.
hint: 'zo' is used before Španielska for easier pronunciation; drop subject pronouns if you like
theme: a map of Europe — naming countries in Slovak

en: We live in Germany.
hint: locative of Nemecko → Nemecku; 'v' triggers locative case
theme: a map of Europe — naming countries in Slovak

en: Do you live in Poland or in the Czech Republic?
sk: Bývaš v Poľsku alebo v Českej republike?
altSk: Ty bývaš v Poľsku alebo v Českej republike?
Bývate v Poľsku alebo v Českej republike?
hint: 'Českej republike' is locative of 'Česká republika' — adjective and noun both change; 'bývate' is the polite/plural form
focus: locative — v + country, question word order, adjective-noun agreement in locative
theme: a map of Europe — naming countries in Slovak

en: Jana comes from France.
hint: nationality noun (f.): Francúzka — simplest A1 way to express origin
focus: country names in locative with 'vo/v' or nationality noun
theme: talking about which countries your classmates come from

en: My classmate is French.
hint: 'Francúz' = French man (nationality noun, masculine); 'Francúzka' = French woman
theme: talking about which countries your classmates come from

en: Where does your classmate live?
hint: 'býva' and 'žije' both mean 'lives/stays'; 'tvoj' = your (informal sg)
theme: talking about which countries your classmates come from

en: My classmates live in Italy, not in Spain.

Dobre si spala včera v noci?

theme: saying you don't have or don't do something

en: At what time does the bus go?
hint: Use 'o koľkej' for asking time; autobus is nominative subject

en: The tram runs from eight to four.
sk: Električka jazdí od ôsmej do štvrtej.
altSk: Električka ide od ôsmej do štvrtej.
Električka premáva od ôsmej do štvrtej.
hint: od + locative, do + locative: od ôsmej do štvrtej — standard time range formula

en: Yesterday the bus did not come on time.
hint: Past tense of prísť → prišiel (irregular, like ísť→išiel); neprišiel = negation; včera = time expression

en: Did the last tram already go?
hint: Past tense question without 'či' — rising intonation; išla = fem. past of ísť; už = already

en: It is half past seven.
hint: 'Half past seven' in Slovak is 'pol ôsmej' — literally 'half of the eighth'

en: The film starts at quarter past eight.
sk: Film začína o štvrť na deväť.
hint: 'Quarter past eight' = 'štvrť na deväť' (quarter to nine in Slovak counting)
focus: quarter past: štvrť na + cardinal (štvrť na deväť)

en: Was the meeting at quarter to three?
sk: Bolo stretnutie o trištvrte na tri?
altSk: Bolo to stretnutie o trištvrte na tri?
hint: 'Quarter to three' = 'trištvrte na tri' — literally 'three-quarters to three'
focus: quarter to: trištvrte na + cardinal (trištvrte na tri)

en: The bus did not leave at half past ten.
altSk: Ten autobus neodišiel o pol jedenástej.
hint: Past tense negative + 'pol jedenástej' for half past ten; 'odísť' → 'odišiel'
focus: half hour in past tense negative: pol + ordinal (pol jedenástej)
